content.comment_body: Hello, I've been attempting to set up a MODBUS TCP connection between a [product_name] controller (version [version_no]) and an Arduino Mega with an EN28J60 Ethernet adapter for the entire day, but haven't had success yet. My objective is to expand the I/O using the Arduino Mega; for instance, if I configure a network output on the [product_name], the Arduino should update a corresponding digital output. Similarly, digital inputs on the Arduino should be visible on the [product_name] through network input. I'm unsure if this integration is achievable, but I'm currently focusing on making the output signal from [product_name] to Arduino work. There's an Arduino library for MODBUS TCP available. Any advice on how to proceed would be appreciated. Kind regards, [user_name]
Can you share what you have tried so far?
I can assist only with the [product_name] controller. I don't have experience with Arduino or the specific ethernet adapter.

Hi, I've uploaded a screenshot showing some settings and a test program. My input is a basic NO switch. On the Arduino side, I wrote a program for a blinking LED with variable frequency depending on the switch state sent from the [product_name]. I'm not certain if my MODBUS configuration (with [product_name] as server) is correct. The Arduino MODBUS library says it runs only as a slave, but it's unclear if 'slave' means client or server in this context.
For MODBUS, slave is equivalent to server, while client is master.

Therefore, the [product_name] controller acts as the client and Arduino as the server. This means [product_name] can only request info from Arduino, such as reading a value from an analog input. Is it also possible to send data from the [product_name] to Arduino? For example, like in PROFINET setups, where both controller and device can share outputs and inputs mutually.
The client directs the communication—it can both read and write. The server (slave) responds to client commands and performs requested operations.

Hello, If you've configured [product_name] as a Modbus server, and you want to read or write I/O directly, you don't need to use VM-memory. You'll want Arduino to read DI1 from [product_name] directly, which accesses the Input1 status. To control output 1, set coil 8193. The unit ID for [product_name] should be 255. Also, a program in [product_name] is necessary to switch it to RUN mode. Hope that helps.

Hi, thanks for your reply. My main goal is to activate digital outputs on Arduino from the [product_name]. For instance, I could set a VM bit in [product_name], and have Arduino read it as a MODBUS coil—though I'm not fully sure if that's the right approach. I'll have time to run more tests over the weekend. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are working to set up MODBUS TCP communication between a [product_name] controller and an Arduino Mega to extend I/O capabilities. There is some confusion about MODBUS terms (slave vs server, client vs master), as well as setup details for integrating the [product_name] controller with third-party devices. Users need clearer configuration instructions and use case explanations for direct MODBUS TCP interaction between [product_name] and Arduino.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want straightforward guidance to configure the [product_name] controller to exchange digital signals with Arduino via MODBUS TCP, making it possible to control Arduino outputs from the [product_name] controller and read inputs from Arduino, with easy-to-follow instructions and terminology.
